title: Token Chronicle Costboard — session-aware timeline & export UX
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Prototype a compact, session-oriented cost analytics view in Redwood Console that surfaces token-level attribution mapped to a timeline (the ‘Token Chronicle Costboard’). The view combines a stacked per-role token burn line, segment-level attribution (prompt / assistant / function), and a heatmap for token density over session time. Users can: (1) inspect which prompt segments drive cost spikes, (2) filter by model variant and quantization profile, (3) generate exportable artifacts (CSV, JSONL, compressed per-session bundle) with role-aware schemas, and (4) open the pricing rules editor to simulate alternate ratecards for cost impact. The prototype must integrate with existing rollout UI patterns (canary vs stable) to show how cost changes flow across a rollout. This ticket covers design explorations, an interactive Figma prototype, and a staged handoff doc for PM/Eng to implement the export schema and backend endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive Figma prototype with timeline scrubber and role-based stacked area chart
Export modal that supports CSV column presets and a JSONL per-message mode
Pricing rules editor mock that toggles per-token rates and shows delta in UI
Design spec for API contract for /sessions/:id/cost-breakdown including sample payloads
Sign-off from PM (Lena Ortiz) and Eng lead (Kai Nakamura) on feasibility and rollout integration
decisions: Use session-first primary key for timeline to preserve ordering and allow scrubber UX
Default export schema will include: session_id, timestamp_ms, role, token_count, token_type_hint, token_cost_microunits, prompt_segment_id
Show per-role stacked area by default; specialist heatmap collapses beneath for small screens
Price-simulation only runs in-browser for initial prototype to avoid backend rollout work
tradeoffs: In-browser price simulation avoids backend changes but can misrepresent cached KV effects
High-granularity exports (per-token) can be large — include a compressed bundle option and sampling presets
Timeline scrubber needs efficient delta rendering to avoid console jank — engineering recommends virtualized rows for long sessions
dependencies: ENG-39210 (session-cost-api): backend endpoints for per-session breakdown
PM-221: rollout policy UI extension for cost preview
